independent_review.text:
# Independent review: bounded removal of six menu exports

The V3 implementation is supported as an intermediate product/tooling change, with its stale source-proof obligations left open and without claiming full verification or admission. Patch SHA-256 34d1493147473f55c124a98422b6a0d14af943f802823fe165573fd88750b951; manifest SHA-256 d7c4c9c2fddb4bc73b18b563153bcec4b3bd7f455e3c74ffd337468eef0c46ca. Strict cached application to 767bcbcc484722759f667dbe709ade31f5040b82 produced independently reconstructed tree add749ec84415cb26e5b532c34cda28835187465; strict check also passed on the author's f522ad64 after its unrelated intervening changes. I rehashed all four before/after source files and 25 retained artifact entries. V3 differs from V2 only in a test-only explanation of JIT metadata reflection.

Tagged Material16 legacy primary `public-api.ts` does not export `_MatLegacyMenuBase`, `_MatLegacyMenuTriggerBase`, `_MatLegacyMenuContentBase`, the two legacy-named scroll-strategy factory/provider aliases or `LEGACY_MENU_PANEL_TOP_PADDING`. The tag did export the scroll token and its module used the peer provider. The patch removes exactly those six addon aliases and their six corresponding API allowlist entries; MatCommonModule and every other allowlist entry/signature disposition remain unchanged. The owned base classes, module provider, scroll factory, templates and styles remain in implementation. No judgment about unsearched external users or the separately owned MatCommonModule contract follows.

The independently examined packed declaration diff removes only those six public export names, now-unreferenced factory/provider/constant declarations and an unused import; the public menu classes still extend locally declared base classes. Candidate versus baseline menu FESM differs only in the export statement. I rehashed the candidate tar f4e7efb14265f08bb6395fa5cd67515ee7853fda8d90252b21c601589b831b7c, compared all 512 installed package files with its tar members, and independently reran the strict consumer typecheck, including six `@ts-expect-error` missing-name controls, on the retained installed package. A public `importProvidersFrom(MatLegacyMenuModule)` synthetic Angular application environment resolved the actual shared scroll token and invoked reposition twice; a separately supplied noop strategy was rejected. This is public DI in a synthetic server fixture, not browser rendering.

The actual packed motion observer ran nine finite state cases, classified four injection requests against the public `MatLegacyMenu` superclass anchor, and rejected both a foreign public export and a modified prototype; I independently reran it. The revised source-emitted menu caller probe retained its existing provider/query checks, corrects its stale item-token expectation to the actual owned item token, and the retained dev/prod observations plus noop mutant are bounded source-JIT evidence. Its additional module-provider observation still uses test-only `__annotations__` metadata reflection: this is not a stable public Angular metadata API. The separate packed public-DI check above provides the stable public provider behavior evidence; neither source-JIT fixture nor it establishes browser or AOT gate completion. The three input/virtual-store/project lock fingerprints before and after match; these are not a complete dependency-closure freeze. Bounded Cyph TS/TSX/JS/JSX/HTML/CSS/SCSS searches found no exact removed-name use; dynamic, generated and other consumers remain outside scope.

Stale proofs are explicitly unresolved rather than refreshed: the old motion observation is rejected by the new owner schema, the authored/menu caller and shared motion/allowlist source-bound capsules need owner-coordinated successors, and all eight existing menu C04 decisions reference the previous public-barrel hash (the 4b prose also explicitly describes the now-removed aliases as present). An independent exact-767 production-checker comparison showed the insufficient/evidence union rise from 825 to 833, precisely those eight menu SHAs reopening, and no SHA newly becoming sufficient; both overall admissions stayed incomplete. `cli-comparison.json` SHA-256 d2aa64aa77c5b4bc6635fb19abb29f51ec3e78aaa15c9b81592b5908f19784c5. This is bounded evidence that those eight source checks fail closed, not a universal proof about every source authority.

The maintained `tests.test_api_owned_motion_context` run against V3 did not pass: 3 of 4 tests passed, while its existing menu receipt was rejected with `owned motion constructor owner identity evidence incomplete`. The failure is expected from the schema change but remains a real failing check until its source-proof successor is generated and independently qualified; `maintained-motion-test.log` SHA-256 dde34a160a985cd76918f204e8d5e5d3d6568703cb0f8445143c88775561fae4. This review supports an intermediate commit only if that failure and all stale authorities remain explicitly tracked. No full historical suite, native browser run, full API/C04 gate, 21.x, security clearance, full admission or release qualification is claimed. No canonical files were changed and no installation was run in this review.
